narr: Nocturnal thunderstorms caused flash flooding early in the morning. Other storms developed later in the day with more flash flooding.
ev: A stream gauge on Cherry Creek reported a 3.61 foot rise.
Several reports of over-flowing drainages, rocks, and debris on the roads making them impassable.
Street flooding was reported in Cottonwood with water flowing over the road.
Heavy rain caused Dry Creek to rise 2.5 feet in a flash flood.
Highway US 60 was closed between Mile Post 384 and Vernon due to flash flooding.

Flood waters in the Paria River reached the river gauge near the Colorado River at 0500 and rose 3.3 feet in 15 minutes. The flood waters likely traveled down this slot canyon from Utah through the early morning hours.

Water in Black Canyon Creek had receded across Maren Avenue to 6 to 8 inches by the time the Sherriff officer saw it in the morning. High water marks indicated that it was much higher at the flood crest.
Street flooding was reported in and around Prescott Valley. One road in Prescott Valley was washed out due to the flooding.
Heavy rain over the Rafael Fire caused a 4 foot rise on the Verde River at Clarkdale (an increase of at least 1,300 CFS).
Law Enforcement reported that Highway 191 was close due to flooding in St Johns at Water Street. There was 12 to 18 inches of water covering the road.
